themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Surge
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights spiked dramatically this week to 13 reports—a 1633% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.8 complaints per week—suggesting an emerging or accelerating public safety concern requiring immediate investigation into whether this reflects new dealing activity, enforcement changes, or community reporting patterns.
evidence: 13 drug activity complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.24, highest statistical significance in dataset)
1633% spike represents 16x normal complaint volume in single week
Signal too recent and acute to have prior news coverage or community board documentation
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct about whether complaints reflect new street-level dealing or increased community reporting; map complaint locations to identify hotspots
Talk to residents in high-complaint blocks about what they're observing and whether they feel the neighborhood has changed in the past 1-2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped 233% this week to 40 reports—compared to a 12-week average of 12 per week—indicating potential infrastructure failures, breaks, or service disruptions affecting multiple blocks and warranting urgent Department of Environmental Protection investigation.
evidence: 40 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs 12 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.84)
233% spike indicates acute infrastructure event rather than chronic problem
No recent news coverage suggests story may not yet be reported publicly
reporting_angles: File FOIL request with DEP for emergency work orders filed this week in CD 302; map complaint locations to identify whether failures are clustered
Contact DEP spokesperson about cause of spike and estimated service restoration timeline; identify affected blocks to find impacted residents

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints surged 500% this week to 21 reports—versus a baseline of 3.5 per week—suggesting either coordinated vandalism, contractor negligence during development work, or seasonal property owner clearance; aligns with 327% spike in overgrown tree complaints last week, indicating broader tree management crisis.
evidence: 21 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs 3.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.61)
8 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs 1.9 average (z-score: 5.82)—convergent signal of tree infrastructure stress
1,236 building permits filed in last 90 days (108 new buildings, 883 alterations) may indicate contractor-caused damage during development
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 tree damage complaints with active DOB permits to see if damage is clustered around construction sites; interview Parks Department about enforcement actions
Investigate whether developers or contractors are illegally removing or damaging protected trees during renovation/demolition work; identify repeat violators

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Outage Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints peaked 2 weeks ago at 37 reports—265% above the 10.1 weekly baseline—and remain elevated, suggesting either systematic infrastructure degradation, recent storm damage, or contractor work affecting public safety and pedestrian visibility district-wide.
evidence: 37 street light complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs 10.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.3)
265% spike indicates acute event rather than chronic maintenance backlog
No recent news mentions suggest story may have been under-reported
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Environmental Protection about what caused the peak 2 weeks ago (weather event, contractor work, major outage) and current repair status
Document which blocks have non-functional street lights and how long residents have waited for repairs; gather safety data (crime, accidents) from dark areas

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Stress
themes_detail.summary: Electrical system complaints spiked 264% to 10 reports 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 2.8 per week, suggesting potential power delivery issues, transformer failures, or wiring problems in aging Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights housing stock or construction-related electrical damage.
evidence: 10 electrical complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 4.06)
Convergent with water system and street light spikes, suggesting possible weather event or utility infrastructure stress 3 weeks ago
reporting_angles: Check Con Edison service advisories or outage logs from 3 weeks ago to determine if spike correlates with known infrastructure event or weather damage
Interview Con Edison about whether aging infrastructure in these neighborhoods is experiencing increased failure rates; identify blocks most affected
